name: EVgo, Inc.

profile.description: EVgo operates a U.S. network of public DC fast-charging stations for EV drivers. It also serves OEMs, rideshare and autonomous-vehicle fleets through dedicated charging and charging-as-a-service, and offers EVSE development, installation and maintenance through its eXtend business [3]. Revenue grew from $13.0M in 2020 to $384.1M in 2025 [3]. In 2026, charging network revenue is growing about 18-19%, while total revenue swings with lumpy eXtend and AV fleet lease items: Q1 +45% to ~$110M, Q2 -16% to $82.6M [1][2]. The shares trade at $1.24, against a 52-week range of $0.98-4.11, for a ~$389M market cap [3].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Beyond public charging, EVgo has opened distinct new revenue streams: the eXtend white-label build-and-operate business (FY2026 guidance raised to $90-95M) and dedicated charging for autonomous-vehicle and rideshare fleets, which drove Q1 2026 sales-type lease revenue [1][2]. These helped scale revenue from $13.0M in 2020 to $384.1M in 2025 [3]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI-driven savings were found. Market Share (1/2): EVgo is a leading public DC fast-charging operator, with charging-network revenue up 19% to $61.4M in Q2 2026, but no share-of-market data was found and Tesla's Supercharger network competes for the same drivers [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Management guides FY2026 revenue to $410-470M and says Q4 will be the largest quarter, but has not given dated next-generation products [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D expense is reported [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): EVgo's purpose of accelerating transportation electrification through fast charging is clear and connects to a broader goal, but it is not distinctive among charging peers and has not been validated by profitable execution [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community-investment program with dollar amounts was found. The FY2025 10-K treats ESG only as a risk factor, and Sustainalytics rates its ESG management as weak [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. The company added its first Chief People Officer in 2025 amid a 'rapidly evolving charging landscape' [5]. Insider Buying (1/2): Insider activity is minimal and balanced. FMP shows zero open-market purchases and zero open-market sales from Q4 2025 through Q3 2026, with only grant and withholding transactions [3].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on 7 growth-sleeve metrics (10 weight units): weighted sum 2.86/10, rounded to 3. EVgo is an Up-C structure: common stockholders' equity is -$20.5M, but total equity including the $330.0M noncontrolling interest is $309.6M. Derived D/E is 134.2% (total debt $415.6M / total equity), scoring 0.72. Derived ROE is -39.6% (TTM consolidated net loss from continuing operations of $122.7M / total equity), scoring 0.0 at 2x weight [3]. The provider's ROE of +41% is excluded as an artifact of dividing a loss by negative common equity. Q2 2026 revenue fell 15.7% YoY ($82.6M vs $98.0M), scoring 0.14. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 96.6% scores 1.0 at 2x weight. Forward P/E is negative (derived from FY2027 consensus EPS of -$0.43), scoring 0.0. The TTM net margin of -13.5% scores 0.0, and the forward PEG is negative/not meaningful, scoring 0.0 at 2x weight [3]. Liquidity: ~3.66M shares/day × $1.24 ≈ $4.5M/day, above the $1M floor but thin.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9, IMMUNE): EVgo sells electrons through physical DC fast chargers at real-world sites, and builds and maintains charging hardware through eXtend. AI cannot substitute for this, and searches found no analyst commentary flagging AI displacement risk [1][2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Autonomous-vehicle fleets are a quantifiable revenue source. A dedicated AV/rideshare fleet customer's sales-type lease drove much of Q1 2026's 45% revenue jump and is reported as 'AV and ancillary revenue' in the 10-Q [1].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, EVgo has a cause people can rally around: electrifying transportation. It has kept investing through persistent losses (capex is ~35% of revenue) and expanded into eXtend and AV fleets as the market shifted [1][3]. However, it remains a young, cash-burning company with a free-cash-flow yield of -50%. Its record has not yet been tested in a way that shows whether the cause or the capital markets drive its decisions [3].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Enabling the shift to electric transportation is service-oriented, idealistic and bigger than any single product, and it underpins the company's expansion into fleets, AVs and eXtend [1][3]. It has not yet been tested by decades of execution or survived a leadership change at a mature stage.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The 2023 CEO handoff from Cathy Zoi to Badar Khan was planned and orderly. Glassdoor shows 3.6/5 from 76 reviews, 81% CEO approval and 63% would-recommend, in line with the industry average of 3.7 [4][5]. That indicates adequate, not exceptional, trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that frames rivals such as Tesla's Supercharger network or ChargePoint as teachers. Strategy disclosures focus on EVgo's own network growth [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): EVgo has moved from a pure public-charging network toward a services model: eXtend white-label buildouts, dedicated AV/rideshare depots and charging-as-a-service [1][3]. These are adjacent extensions of its core rather than a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management continues to fund network buildout despite losses. Capex runs at about 35% of revenue, and it has taken on $415.6M of total debt to keep expanding rather than retrench [3]. Whether this is courage or capital-markets dependence will be judged by its path to positive adjusted EBITDA (FY2026 guide: -$20M to +$20M) [1].

investment_thesis: Bull case: EVgo's core charging-network revenue is compounding at 18-19% (Q2 2026: $61.4M), autonomous-vehicle fleets are emerging as a new dedicated-charging customer class, and eXtend guidance was raised to $90-95M [1][2]. Consensus sees revenue reaching ~$519M in 2027 and ~$700M in 2028, with adjusted EBITDA scaling to ~$113M and ~$185M. At ~$389M market cap, the stock trades below 1x TTM sales [3].
thesis_continued: Bear case: EVgo is still burning cash. TTM free cash flow is about -$1.38/share against a $1.24 price, and consensus expects GAAP losses through 2029 [3]. Reported revenue is lumpy (Q2 2026 -16% YoY) because of one-off eXtend and AV lease items, and the shares fell 12.7% on Q2 results despite a sales beat [2]. Common equity is negative, debt is rising ($415.6M including leases), and the ~70% decline from the $4.11 52-week high signals dilution and financing risk [3].
key_catalysts: Q4 2026, which management expects to be the largest revenue quarter, and delivery within the $410-470M FY2026 revenue and -$20M to +$20M adjusted EBITDA guidance [1][2]
Additional dedicated AV and rideshare fleet contracts following the Q1 2026 sales-type lease [1]
eXtend growth to the raised $90-95M guidance, adding capital-light services revenue [2]
key_risks: Funding and dilution risk: negative FCF of ~$193M TTM and negative common equity with a ~$389M market cap [3]
EV adoption slowdown or loss of policy support reducing charger utilization
Revenue lumpiness and customer concentration in the AV/ancillary and eXtend lines, as shown by the Q2 2026 -16% decline [2]
